summary: Yakima County lookout built in 1933 with an L-4 cab; removed or destroyed in 1968 (sources differ). The Goat Peak trail still has views; no source describes the site now.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and Forest Lookouts say removed in 1968; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1968; Willhite cites a 1971 USGS report of a fire-destroyed house; Visit Rainier says dismantled in the 1960s. The story reports the disagreement without choosing one.
Forest Lookouts names the Snoqualmie National Forest; firelookout.com names the Wenatchee National Forest, originally the Snoqualmie. The story gives both names.

sources.title: American Ridge (Goat Peak) Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: Built year (1933) and the 1955 rescue are consistent across three sources. Fate is disputed: removed (Register, Forest Lookouts) versus destroyed (firelookout.com, Willhite) and a 1971 fire report; the story does not choose. Brief elevation 1973.0 m was not checked against a source: the 1955 article gives 6,494 feet (about 1,980 m), so the editor may want to confirm the register value; no correction proposed. Brief kind 'ground' comes from the firelookout.org Washington index; Willhite mentions a storage shed 20 feet below the cab, so the cab's support is not described. Access 'public' is inferred from a hiking guide, not a Forest Service page. Do not confuse with other Goat Peak or Goat Ridge lookouts in the same sources (Chelan NF Goat Peak, Lewis County Goat Ridge); the Substack and TrailChick pages describe a different Goat Peak and were not used.
